author: root/coordinator

checks.description: Prove exact U-Boot recovery dispatch and unarmed/default fallback with explicit one-shot marker and payload binding.
Prove ordered durable staging, exact target/source admission and fail-closed prewrite/postopen interruption semantics without automatic retry.
Exercise actual RAM writer/controller success, refusal and normal return in disposable QEMU; default SD/A-B paths stay unchanged.
Read-only physical recovery handoff captures live identity, marker/fallback and return without whole-device target open.
Separately reviewed H12 full physical write/readback/next boot with exact target, artifact and recovery.

constraints.text: Integrate the marker and payload checks with the exact compiled dispatcher and RAUC bootmeth. Test valid, exhausted, malformed and redundant-environment states. Preserve the original recovery UI for every unarmed, absent, malformed or mismatched case; isolated selector probes alone do not satisfy this check.

Use disposable media and synthetic identity for staging and fault tests. Verify exact recovery-partition identity, signed job, image/map, payload hashes and measured space before arming. Preserve the original recovery files and make the marker durably unusable before the first target open. A prewrite interruption must retain normal boot or recovery; an uncertain postopen result must never retry automatically.

Run the actual RAM writer and one-shot controller through the proposed handoff in disposable QEMU. Check full write, flush, readback, GPT result and the next normal-slot boot after replacement of the temporary recovery script and environment. Exercise refusal and interruption paths, and keep the default SD diagnostic and A/B updater unchanged. Measure final staging space and boot-memory use; keep raw 8 GB artifacts off the space-limited development VM.

Treat read-only physical handoff and attended physical reimage as separate later H12 decisions. Before either physical boot-policy operation or write, require exact current target and artifact evidence, a recovery plan, applicable owner authorization and immediate independent high-consequence review. Offline success grants no physical or release authority.

decision.rationale: Decision 0018 and the owner's standing writerless goal authorize a bounded offline prototype. The prior needs-research decision identified dispatcher behavior, capacity and selector semantics as unknowns. The 2026-09-27 research now supplies disposable U-Boot sandbox traces for exhausted and corrupt A/B states, a measured recovery-image free-space budget, load-address analysis, and isolated marker/FIT selector results. The completed trusted-writer feature supplies a synthetic controller-integrated QEMU write, readback, GPT check and refusal path. These justify implementing urh-01 through urh-03. Durable marker consumption, ordered staging, the exact integrated recovery handoff and normal boot after image replacement remain required acceptance results of that implementation; they are not prerequisites to permitting an offline prototype. The isolated selector probe and image measurements do not establish those results or physical behavior. Approval covers only disposable offline work. urh-04 and urh-05 remain separate H12 hardware gates requiring exact target and artifact review, recovery planning, applicable owner authorization and immediate independent high-consequence review. No printer contact, physical boot-policy change or eMMC write is approved.

evidence.limitations: Only sandbox selection of a test marker is proven. The FIT is nonbootable; no RAM writer, marker consumption, QEMU write, live board or physical recovery UI was tested.
evidence.method: Run tests/uboot_recovery_handoff.py against U-Boot 2026.07 sandbox with a disposable 256 MiB GPT regular file, FAT A/B boot slots, ext4 recovery, redundant raw MMC environment and real RAUC bootmeth. Retained build/urh-selector-v5/result.json SHA-256 efdf6ceb63f8c997b3357637156fe463a059c235bd1ff5d62832adf443f16245; nine case logs cover armed, absent, malformed, mismatched payload, valid slot, invalid order, one and both corrupt environment copies. Review delivered diff 48edc50..b1c92aa; workflow claim was recorded after the already-committed test.

tasks.title: Prove fail-closed recovery selector and one-shot trigger

verification.rationale: At clean HEAD 4dec9ad, I reviewed the full delivery and submission diffs, source, evidence document, result and nine sandbox logs. The recorded document, source and result hashes match. The test compiles the exact boot-dispatch.cmd and exercises RAUC with redundant MMC environment copies on a disposable 256 MiB image. An exhausted A/B state with the expected marker and FIT reaches SV08_TEST_WRITER_SELECTED; a valid A slot boots the slot. Absent, short and same-length wrong markers, a changed FIT, invalid boot order and both corrupt environment copies reach the original-recovery test marker instead. The wrong-marker and wrong-FIT logs show explicit crc32 -v mismatch errors before recovery is sourced. One corrupt environment copy still selects the writer when armed. This passes the bounded offline urh-01 dispatch check. The original recovery UI is represented by an echo script, and the FIT is nonbootable; actual UI execution, marker consumption, RAM-writer handoff and hardware behavior remain for urh-02/03 and later gates.

tasks.blocker: Reviewed clean HEAD 69b147349e4db23939af3c777324fb3ce2be198c against the approved decision, run base c111d4f, full changed-file list, implementation, tests and submitted evidence. The recorded source and evidence-document hashes match; the worktree is clean. urh-03 remains unmet: the QEMU harness starts the writer with external -kernel and -initrd arguments. It does not execute the staged recovery selector's FIT boot, so the required writer boot through the proposed handoff is unproven. The later normal-slot run also starts a separate QEMU snapshot. The reported postopen interruption was inspected but not rebooted, and the implemented after-bulk and after-first-env retry tests have no submitted execution results. urh-02's fault cases check staged files and journal states, but do not establish boot fallback at every interruption point. Physical H616 U-Boot-to-FIT execution remains absent and cannot be inferred from these offline results; urh-04 and urh-05 remain separate hardware gates. The named Beelink result JSON and serial logs could not be inspected because the Beelink hostname did not resolve, so their reported hashes and contents were not independently confirmed. Supply integrated handoff and fault-path execution evidence, then resubmit.

evidence.limitations: Disposable regular-file and loop ext4 only; no installed eMMC target admission, live boot-policy change, physical fsync/power-cut or H616 U-Boot-to-FIT handoff tested.
evidence.method: Reviewed signed staging and loop-backed partition-five admission; ran 20 focused unit tests and root-owned mounted-stage-v3, checked journal fault states, compiled selector/FIT payloads, exact GPT, target device/inode binding and both redundant environment copies. Mounted-stage result SHA-256 b26c472cfec4b642d2b7f3c03522cec089f2d7d080d351985f1a0520c17cefe3. The integrated split-controller QEMU success used the same stager and produced result SHA-256 eea94030b619b9b7b58121cd89185483f4ac1beea9d2b17c9e254fb64c0842fa.

evidence.limitations: QEMU virt loads the verified FIT kernel/initramfs externally after separate U-Boot sandbox selector checks; it does not emulate physical H616 U-Boot handing control to FIT. Normal boot is a separate snapshot launch on the same target. One atomic page-allocation warning occurred in the passing 1 GiB run. The partial target was inspected read-only but not rebooted; physical eMMC, printer services and release remain untested.
evidence.method: Ran exact-v5-source 1 GiB QEMU virt with staged writer payload, one-shot NFS controller, separate emulated network/target controllers and 32 GB sparse target. Guest and independent host full-image SHA-256, six GPT records, claim and final redundant environments passed; result SHA-256 eea94030b619b9b7b58121cd89185483f4ac1beea9d2b17c9e254fb64c0842fa. Tampered signed-job refusal result SHA-256 8e8b1226836474fdcfb24a9325002a115852a70d3635fe96cd38d8a10e9b440b. An interrupted shared-controller postopen run left both old exhausted environments CRC-valid and the marker absent; serial SHA-256 9a2f701c199ae0e13eee0a3f1a6f36c9680680045ded35c066f08ba9b84881c0. A subsequent production-initramfs snapshot boot of the successful target reached sv08-prepare, multi-user.target and login; result SHA-256 9b14aec0da6571fb5db6d3fe891bfe63d1d8190ed9c377f4bde7f367f35d5068.
